description:
kith-core/src/error.rs line 27: pub enum KithError has a variant Jmap(jmap_types::JmapError). This exposes the jmap_types crate's public type directly in kith-core's error API.

Consequences:
1. Any change to jmap_types::JmapError (field rename, variant add/remove) is a breaking change for KithError consumers even if kith-core's own API is unchanged.
2. Callers that match on KithError::Jmap(e) must import or depend on jmap_types directly, even though jmap_types is meant to be an implementation detail of kith-core.
3. From<jmap_types::JmapError> for KithError (line 34) and the Jmap variant together mean the boundary between kith-core's error model and jmap-types' error model is load-bearing in callers.

The same applies to AuthError: it is a kith-core public error variant (KithError::Auth(AuthError)), and AuthError::WhoIsFailed(String) wraps a String — which is fine — but AuthError is re-exported from kith-core and consumed by kith-jmap, kith-peer, and kithd.

Fix for Jmap leakage: replace KithError::Jmap(jmap_types::JmapError) with KithError::Protocol { error_type: String, description: Option<String> } or a kith-owned opaque JmapMethodError newtype. This isolates callers from jmap_types version bumps.
title: kith-core: KithError wraps jmap_types::JmapError — third-party type leakage
